skill.name: tech-writing-proofread
skill.description: Proofreads English technical documents for language, terminology, and structure issues, returning specific suggestions and reasons without rewriting the document.
skill.summary: Review technical writing with an itemized correction checklist, uncertainty flags, and issue counts.
skill.author: alapha888

content.value_statement: Technical drafts can contain language errors and inconsistent terminology that make instructions harder to follow. This skill provides specific corrections, reasons, and issue counts while preserving the authorial voice.
actual_capabilities: Identify spelling errors, doubled words, grammar mistakes, and inconsistent punctuation.
Compare terminology across a document and suggest the most frequent form for each concept.
Check inline code formatting and official casing for product names.
Flag passive voice, filler words, nonparallel headings, and unexpanded acronyms.
Return an Original / Suggestion / Reason checklist with line numbers or short quotes and verification flags.
Summarize the total number of issues and their category distribution.
limitations: Designed for English technical writing, not multilingual proofreading.
Does not verify technical facts; suspected errors are flagged for confirmation.
Does not rewrite complete paragraphs or produce a replacement document.
Uses a single review pass and does not guarantee an error-free result.

use_cases.title: Review a README
use_cases.description: Find language errors, inconsistent product casing, and unclear procedural wording before publishing repository documentation.

use_cases.title: Check an API reference
use_cases.description: Review terminology, grammatical precision, acronym expansion, and parallel headings without changing technical claims.

use_cases.title: Polish a technical tutorial
use_cases.description: Identify filler words, sentence errors, and inconsistent instructions while preserving a conversational voice.

prompt_templates.title: Proofread a short passage
prompt_templates.prompt: Proofread this English technical passage: [paste text]. Return an Original / Suggestion / Reason checklist and issue counts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a short technical draft.

prompt_templates.title: Review README instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Proofread this README in one pass: [paste README]. Check grammar, product casing, inline code formatting, and numbered steps. Preserve the existing voice.

prompt_templates.title: Check API terminology
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API reference: [paste reference]. Build a terminology list and flag inconsistent names, nonparallel headings, and unexpanded acronyms. Mark uncertain claims [verify].
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: check consistency across a reference document.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a complete tutorial
prompt_templates.prompt: Proofread this complete tutorial: [paste tutorial]. Check all six review categories, preserve its conversational tone, and avoid paragraph rewrites. Cite lines or short quotes. End with category counts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine language, terminology, and structural checks.

output_examples.input: The system call the callback. Examples are available on github.
output: 1. [Grammar] Original: The system call the callback. Suggestion: The system calls the callback. Reason: Singular subject requires calls.
2. [Proper noun] Original: github. Suggestion: GitHub. Reason: Use official product casing.

output_examples.input: Register a callback function. The callback function handles errors. The callback handles completion. Simply invoke the handler.
output: 1. [Terminology] Original: The callback handles completion. Suggestion: The callback function handles completion. Reason: Use the most frequent term consistently.
2. [Style] Original: Simply invoke the handler. Suggestion: Invoke the handler. Reason: Remove filler.

best_practices: Provide the complete document so terminology and tone can be checked consistently.
Identify whether the draft is a tutorial, API reference, blog post, or README.
Review each suggestion and confirm items marked [verify] before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Requesting complete paragraph rewrites instead of specific proofreading suggestions.
Treating suspected factual errors as verified corrections.
Requesting repeated polishing passes without a defined stopping point.

faq.question: What kinds of documents does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews English technical documents, including READMEs, tutorials, API references, and technical blog drafts.

faq.question: Does it rewrite my document?
faq.answer: No. It provides specific corrections and reasons while preserving the existing voice and avoiding complete paragraph rewrites.

faq.question: Does it check technical accuracy?
faq.answer: It flags suspected factual errors for verification. It does not establish technical correctness or silently change uncertain claims.

faq.question: How does it handle inconsistent terminology?
faq.answer: It identifies multiple names for the same concept and recommends the most frequent form in the document.

faq.question: What does the output include?
faq.answer: An Original / Suggestion / Reason checklist, line numbers or short quotes, verification flags, and issue counts by category.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
